It all started with an idea at Block in 2013. Initially built to take the pain out of peer-to-peer payments, Cash App has gone from a simple product with a single purpose to a dynamic ecosystem, developing unique financial products, including Afterpay/Clearpay, to provide a better way to send, spend, invest, borrow and save to our 50+ million monthly active customers. We want to redefine the world’s relationship with money to make it more relatable, instantly available, and universally accessible.

Today, Cash App has thousands of employees working globally across office and remote locations, with a culture geared toward innovation, collaboration and impact. We’ve been a distributed team since day one, and many of our roles can be done remotely from the countries where Cash App operates. No matter the location, we tailor our experience to ensure our employees are creative, productive, and happy.

The Role

The Block Ecosystem Partnerships team leads product partnerships, business development, and commercialization for Afterpay, Cash App, and Square. We develop partnerships that extend the capabilities and reach of our products across the payments and technology industries, building relationships with leading companies in payments, finance, and technology.

We’re looking for an experienced business development and partnerships leader to define and own the global strategy for a portfolio of high-impact partnerships and emerging opportunities. You’ll identify where we should invest, shape our approach, and lead execution across teams to turn those opportunities into measurable business results.

A significant part of this role will involve leading multiple zero-to-one initiatives where the product, partnership model, or go-to-market approach may not yet exist. You’ll bring structure to open-ended opportunities, develop the strategic rationale and commercial model, and work with cross-functional leaders to take ideas from initial concept through launch and scale. This requires strong business judgment about which opportunities to pursue, what not to prioritize, and when to change direction.

You’ll work closely with leaders across Afterpay, Cash App, and Square, including Product, Engineering, Sales, Account Management, Marketing, Finance, Compliance, and Legal. Beyond delivering results for your portfolio, you’ll build repeatable approaches that improve how teams develop, launch, and grow partnerships.

You will:

  • Define and own partnership strategy: Set the long-term growth direction for your partnership area. Translate customer needs, payments economics, competitive developments, and emerging technologies into clear priorities, investment recommendations, and execution plans. Balance near-term commercial results with longer-term opportunities, including agentic commerce.
  • Build new opportunities from zero to one: Identify unmet customer and partner needs, develop business cases, and shape new partnership and distribution models. Lead multiple initiatives in parallel, establishing direction where there is no existing playbook.
  • Make commercial and investment decisions: Evaluate market potential, unit economics, strategic fit, and execution requirements. Recommend which opportunities to pursue or decline, with clear tradeoffs, resource needs, and expected returns.
  • Turn early bets into scalable businesses: Define experiments, milestones, and criteria to scale, pivot, or stop. Lead opportunities through partner development, negotiation, integration, launch, and commercialization. Turn successful approaches into repeatable models that other teams and markets can adopt.
  • Own portfolio performance: Take accountability for the commercial outcomes and long-term health of your partnerships. Establish success measures, assess performance, and adapt strategy as products, partner priorities, and market conditions evolve. Coordinate with colleagues working with the same partners to create a coherent global approach.
  • Build executive relationships and lead complex negotiations: Earn trust with senior decision-makers while maintaining effective working relationships across partner organizations. Structure and negotiate agreements that expand distribution, extend product capabilities, and support sustainable economics, including situations where partners may also be competitors.
  • Shape cross-functional priorities and resolve blockers: Translate strategy into clear product dependencies, resource requirements, ownership, and delivery plans. Influence roadmap and investment decisions, resolve competing priorities across teams, and bring clear recommendations to senior leaders when tradeoffs require broader decisions.
  • Commercialize products globally: Develop distribution strategies for business-to-business and business-to-business-to-consumer payment products, including new integrations, upsell, and cross-sell opportunities. Expand our reach through partner platforms while accounting for regional customer, regulatory, and operational requirements.
  • Build practices that scale beyond your portfolio: Establish shared planning cadences, decision frameworks, and accountability across participating teams. Improve how opportunities are evaluated and partnerships are executed. Mentor senior colleagues and other leaders, helping them navigate ambiguity and make stronger strategic and commercial decisions.

Qualifications

  • 12+ years of experience across business development, strategic partnerships, and commercialization, with deep experience in payments or financial technology. Demonstrated ownership of business strategy and commercial outcomes across complex partnerships, products, or markets.
  • A proven track record of building new businesses or partnership models from zero to one. Experience identifying opportunities, developing business cases, shaping product and go-to-market strategy, negotiating complex agreements, and delivering measurable growth.
  • Strong commercial and strategic judgment, including evaluating investment tradeoffs, assessing unit economics, prioritizing resources, and influencing senior leaders on which opportunities to pursue, scale, or stop.
  • Deep knowledge of consumer and business payments, including payments economics, distribution models, and competitive dynamics. Ability to translate market developments and emerging business models into actionable growth strategies.
  • Proven ability to build C-suite relationships and navigate complex organizations. Expert negotiation skills, a strong understanding of commercial contracts, and experience managing dynamics that may be simultaneously cooperative and competitive.
  • Strong product fluency and experience working with multiple Product and Engineering teams for a single partner. Ability to connect customer needs, technical capabilities, integration requirements, and commercial value.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without formal authority, resolve organizational blockers, and secure cross-functional commitment to shared priorities. Experience building repeatable frameworks or operating practices that improve execution beyond your immediate responsibilities.
  • Entrepreneurial ownership and sound decision-making in ambiguous, fast-changing environments. Ability to guide senior colleagues and communicate strategy, risks, and tradeoffs clearly.
  • Willingness to travel, primarily domestically with some international travel.
  • BS/BA required. An MBA or other master’s degree is a plus.

We are looking for a hands-on, detail-oriented accounting professional to join our Regulated Trading & Derivatives accounting team. Working directly with the Global Accounting Lead (CFO), you will help run the books, close, and regulatory reporting for our Swap-dealer and Broker-dealer entities.

This is a builder role. Many of the processes, reconciliations, and controls you will use do not exist yet, and you will help design them. You will work at the intersection of digital asset trading and traditional market regulation (SEC, FINRA, CFTC, NFA), learning how regulatory capital and financial reporting work from the inside. If you like getting into the detail, finding what is broken, and fixing it, this role is for you.

Accounting & Close

  • Prepare journal entries, account reconciliations, and flux analysis for the Broker-dealer and Swap-dealer entities as part of the monthly, quarterly, and year-end close, in accordance with US GAAP.
  • Account for trading activity, derivatives, margin, collateral, and digital asset positions, and reconcile them to clearing, custody, and counterparty statements.
  • Investigate and resolve breaks and open items quickly, and document the root cause so they do not repeat.
  • Support internal and external auditors with schedules, samples, and walkthroughs.

Regulatory Reporting

  • Prepare the supporting schedules and workpapers behind SEC FOCUS reports, CFTC/NFA swap dealer financial reports (CFTC Regulation 23.105), and daily or monthly net capital computations.
  • Help monitor compliance with SEC Rule 15c3-1 (Net Capital) and SEC Rule 15c3-3 (Customer Protection) for the Broker-dealer, and with CFTC Regulation 23.101 (minimum capital) and 23.104 (equity withdrawal restrictions) for the Swap-dealer, and flag early-warning issues promptly.
  • Support the accounting and reconciliation of all derivatives trading activity for uncleared swaps, including initial and variation margin and collateral under the CFTC uncleared margin rules (CFTC Regulations 23.150–23.161).
  • Maintain the weekly regulatory capital model and prepare related internal updates.
  • Support regulatory audits and examinations (SEC, FINRA, CFTC, NFA): pull and tie out schedules, respond to document requests, and help track remediation items.

Build & Improve

  • Help set up the books, chart of accounts, reconciliations, close checklists, and reporting packages for the Swap-dealer and Broker-dealer entities, and contribute to planning if a futures commission merchant (FCM) is added later.
  • Document processes and help design and test internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR) suited to digital asset trading and derivatives.
  • Look for ways to automate manual work in spreadsheets and the ledgering system, and work with Treasury, Trading Operations, Engineering, and Product to get data flowing cleanly.
  • Partner with Compliance, Legal, and Trading to understand the accounting and regulatory effect of new products and trading strategies.
  • Take on special and ad-hoc projects as the team grows.

You may be a fit for this role if you have:

  • Experience: 8+ years of progressive accounting or finance experience, ideally in the finance team of a broker-dealer, swap dealer, FCM, bank, trading firm, or crypto company.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. CPA license or active progress toward one is strongly preferred.
  • Technical accounting: Solid command of US GAAP, including ASC 815 (Derivatives and Hedging) and accounting for trading securities, margin, collateral, and revenue recognition.
  • Trading and derivatives understanding: Exposure to derivatives such as futures, options, and uncleared swaps. You do not need to have run these books yourself, but you should understand how the trades flow into the ledger.
  • Regulatory awareness: Working familiarity with broker-dealer financial reporting (FOCUS, net capital, customer protection) and CFTC/NFA swap dealer requirements (capital, financial reporting, uncleared margin) is a strong plus. We will train you on the rest and support you in earning Series 27 and NFA Series 3 licenses over time.
  • Tools: Advanced Excel skills and comfort with a modern ledger or ERP (such as NetSuite) and close management tools (such as FloQast). Comfort with SQL, Python, or automation tools is a plus.
  • Hands-on and detail-oriented: You tie out numbers, spot what looks wrong, and follow it through to a fix.
  • Builder mindset: You are at ease setting up processes, templates, and controls from a blank page, and you do not wait for a playbook.
  • Can-do attitude: You take ownership, ask good questions, move quickly when deadlines are tight, and stay calm under pressure.
  • Communication: You can explain accounting and regulatory capital topics clearly to non-finance partners in Trading, Product, and Engineering.

Although not a requirement, bonus points if

  • Experience helping stand up or scale a finance function at a broker-dealer or swap dealer.
  • FCM accounting and reporting experience (CFTC Regulation 1.17, Form 1-FR-FCM, customer segregation), useful if an FCM is launched later.
  • Accounting or financial reporting experience with digital assets or crypto derivatives.
  • Familiarity with institutional trading systems, clearing platforms, and modern ledgering software.
  • Interest in the changing regulatory landscape for stablecoins, tokenized assets, and decentralized finance.
  • Prior Series 27 or NFA Series 3 exam progress.

Robinhood is looking for a Director of Corporate Development to help accelerate our roadmap by identifying, vetting, and executing acquisitions, strategic investments, and other transactions. In this role, you will develop a deep understanding of Robinhood's strategic priorities and market landscape, and partner with GMs and senior leadership to identify high-potential opportunities across our existing and future product verticals and geographies. You will work closely with deal sponsors and cross-functional leaders across Robinhood on all aspects of M&A, including business case construction, valuation analysis, deal structuring, negotiation, due diligence, execution, and post-close integration. You will present opportunities to company leadership and the Board of Directors, facilitate key decisions, and provide post-acquisition performance updates. The ideal candidate is strategic, relationship-oriented, analytical, and results-oriented, and thrives at a public company that still operates like a startup.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA or New York, NY offices, with in-person attendance expected 3 days per week.

Today, raw inference usage events, GPU-hour allocations, and tiered per-token pricing rules live across several internal metering pipelines and billing systems that do not always agree, which produces recurring month-end discrepancies between what customers were charged and what they actually consumed, and slows down the process of issuing service credits when GPU faults or capacity outages interrupt a customer's workload. This role closes that gap: reconciling usage data against billing records line by line, maintaining and evolving the pricing models that translate consumption into charges, and calculating fair, well-documented credits when infrastructure failures affect a tenant's jobs. The person who thrives here is comfortable moving between spreadsheets, SQL queries, and billing-platform configuration in the same afternoon, treats a small reconciliation gap as a signal worth chasing rather than a rounding error, and can explain a pricing or credit decision clearly to both an engineer debugging a metering pipeline and a customer disputing an invoice.

Investigate variances between usage logs and invoiced amounts down to the account and job level, tracing them to metering pipeline bugs, pricing misconfigurations, or timing gaps. Document root causes and drive fixes with engineering and finance-systems teams so recurring discrepancies do not reappear the following month.
